Provide step-by-step setup instructions covering environment preparation, running the application with python3 app.py or ./start.sh, and accessing the web interface at http://127.0.0.1:8000. Address common startup issues like port conflicts and Git PATH configuration. Make this accessible to beginners while providing essential technical details.

wiki_catalogs.name: Understanding Git Metrics
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content explaining the core Git metrics calculated by RAT. Define and provide practical examples for each metric type: added/removed lines (code changes per commit), growth (net code accumulation over time), churn (total modifications regardless of direction), modifications (commit frequency analysis), churn rate (modification velocity), and ownership analysis (author contribution distribution). Explain how these metrics are computed from raw git history data, including the SQL aggregation queries used. Detail the different dimensions of analysis (files, directories, repositories, commit sets, authors) and how filters affect metric calculations. Include visual examples showing how metrics change over time and across different repository structures. Address common interpretations and use cases for each metric type.

wiki_overview.content:
# RAT - Repo Analysis Tool: Comprehensive Project Analysis ## 1. Project Introduction **RAT (Repo Analysis Tool)** is a local, offline dashboard that ingests Git repositories and computes comprehensive code metrics including added/removed lines, growth, churn, modifications, churn rate, and ownership analysis for every file, directory, repository, commit set, and author. ### Purpose Statement - **Primary Goal**: Provide developers with deep insights into their codebase evolution through detailed metric analysis - **Target Audience**: Developers, team leads, and technical managers seeking to understand code change patterns, contributor impact, and repository health - **Key Differentiator**: Fully offline operation with no external dependencies beyond Python standard library and Git ### Core Goals and Objectives - **Zero-dependency deployment**: Runs entirely on Python 3.8+ standard library - **Comprehensive metrics**: Calculates growth, churn, frequency, and ownership statistics - **Flexible ingestion**: Supports both remote Git URLs and local zip archives containing `.git` directories - **Real-time feedback**: Background job processing with progress tracking - **Interactive visualization**: Rich web interface with filtering, sorting, and charting capabilities ## 2. Technical Architecture The project follows a clean separation of concerns with distinct layers for HTTP serving, business logic, data access, and frontend presentation. ```mermaid flowchart TD Client[Web Browser] --> API[HTTP Server
app.py] API --> Ingest[Ingestion Engine
ingest.py] API --> Metrics[Metrics Engine
metrics.py] API --> Static[Static Files
static/] Ingest --> DB[(SQLite Database
db.py)] Metrics --> DB Ingest --> Git[Git CLI] Client --> Frontend[Frontend SPA
app.js] Frontend --> API subgraph "Background Processing" Thread[Threading.Thread] --> Ingest end ``` ### Component Breakdown **HTTP Layer (`app.py`)** - Custom `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` implementation with thread-safe request handling - RESTful API endpoints for repository management and metric queries - Static file serving with proper content-type detection and caching headers - Job polling system for background task monitoring **Ingestion Pipeline (`ingest.py`)** - Secure zip extraction with zip-slip attack prevention - Git repository cloning with timeout protection - Single-pass history parsing using optimized `git log` format - Batch database operations for performance optimization **Metrics Engine (`metrics.py`)** - SQL-based aggregation engine with parameterized queries - Flexible filter system supporting date ranges, hash lists, and author filters - Multiple metric categories: file, directory, repository, commit set, and author metrics - Chart data preparation for various visualization types **Data Layer (`db.py`)** - SQLite database with WAL mode for concurrent read/write operations - Schema definition with appropriate indexes for query performance - Connection pooling and transaction management ### Design Patterns 1. **Repository Pattern**: Clean separation between data access and business logic 2. **Observer Pattern**: Progress callbacks during long-running ingestion tasks 3. **Strategy Pattern**: Pluggable metric calculation functions 4. **Factory Pattern**: Dynamic endpoint routing based on URL patterns 5. **Pipeline Pattern**: Sequential ingestion stages with error recovery ## 3. Key Implementation ### Main Entry Points **Server Startup (`app.py`)** - Configurable port binding with automatic fallback mechanism - Database initialization and stale job recovery - ThreadingHTTPServer for concurrent request handling **Database Management (`db.py`)** - Schema migration support with idempotent table creation - Environment-based configuration for data directory location - Connection lifecycle management with proper resource cleanup ### Core Modules **Ingestion Engine (`ingest.py`)** - Secure archive extraction with path traversal protection - Optimized git history parsing using custom binary format - Background job execution with progress tracking and error handling - Automatic cleanup of temporary files and failed ingestion attempts **Metrics Calculator (`metrics.py`)** - Advanced SQL aggregation with multiple join strategies - Author identity resolution with canonical ID mapping - Performance-optimized queries with strategic indexing - Comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messages ### Configuration Approach Environment-based configuration system: - `PORT`: Server port selection with fallback chain - `HOST`: Network interface binding - `DATA_DIR`: Data storage location override ### External Dependencies **Runtime Dependencies:** - Python 3.8+ (standard library only) - Git CLI tool for repository operations **Frontend Dependencies:** - ECharts library for data visualization - No build step or package manager required ### Integration Points **Git Integration:** - Direct subprocess calls to git CLI - Custom output format parsing for optimal performance - Timeout protection against hanging operations **Database Integration:** - SQLite with WAL mode for concurrent access - Parameterized queries for security - Strategic indexing for query performance ```mermaid graph LR App[app.py] --> Ingest[ingest.py] App --> Metrics[metrics.py] App --> DB[db.py] Ingest --> Git[Git CLI] Metrics --> DB Ingest --> DB Static[static/] --> Frontend[Browser] Frontend --> App ``` ## 4. Key Features ### Functionality Overview **Repository Management** - Add repositories from public Git URLs - Upload local zip archives containing `.git` directories - Load sample fixture repository for testing - Delete repositories with cascading cleanup **Metric Analysis** - Repository-level summary statistics - File and directory-level granularity analysis - Author contribution and ownership metrics - Commit timeline and trend analysis - Interactive tree navigation with drill-down capabilities **Advanced Filtering** - Date range filtering (from/to timestamps) - Specific commit hash filtering - Author-based filtering with identity merging - Path-based filtering for specific files/directories ### Implementation Highlights **Performance Optimization (`ingest.py`)** - Batched database inserts (5000 rows per transaction) - Streaming git log parsing to handle large repositories - Memory-efficient token processing for git output - Background threading for non-blocking ingestion **Security Measures (`ingest.py`, `app.py`)** - Zip-slip attack prevention during archive extraction - Input validation and sanitization throughout the pipeline - Path traversal protection in static file serving - Content-Length enforcement for upload limits **User Experience (`static/app.js`)** - Real-time job progress updates via polling - Responsive design with mobile support - Keyboard navigation and accessibility features - Debounced search and filtering interactions ### Feature Architecture ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Pending: Repository Added Pending --> Running: Ingestion Started Running --> Ready: History Parsed Running --> Error: Ingestion Failed Ready --> [*]: Repository Deleted Error --> [*]: Cleanup Complete state Running { [*] --> Cloning Cloning --> Extracting: Clone Complete Extracting --> Parsing: Archive Ready Parsing --> Finalizing: History Loaded Finalizing --> [*]: Status Updated } ``` **Chart System (`metrics.py`)** - Adaptive time bucketing (day/week/month) based on data span - Multiple chart types: churn trends, top files, author distribution - Efficient SQL aggregation for chart data preparation - Consistent data structure across all visualization types **Author Identity Management (`metrics.py`)** - Canonical ID system for author identity resolution - Manual merge functionality for consolidating duplicate identities - Display name and email resolution from canonical records - Impact on all metrics calculations through COALESCE operations Sources: - [README.md](README.md) - [app.py](app.py) - [db.py](db.py) - [ingest.py](ingest.py) - [metrics.py](metrics.py) - [index.html](static/index.html) - [app.js](static/app.js)
